name: 4-coil Shakti: amygdala left + slow hippocampus right (30 min)
summary: Murphy's stereo Shakti session with the alternative 'slow' hippocampal signal on the right temporal lobe and the amygdala signal on the left, offered for users whose standard sessions are 'duds'. Murphy calls the slow signal 'more experimental than the Standard Hippocampal signal'.
setting: Evenings: the vendor says sessions are 'usually better after the sun goes down'. Darkness and quiet (the vendor says effects during a session need darkness and silence); eyes closed, relaxed, without meditating or falling asleep; no meditation, mind machines or drugs at the same time.
schedule: Vendor's Shakti rules: at most every 72 h or once a week, never on consecutive days; a series of 3 or 6 sessions, then a 21-day break; try a session 2-3 times before changing it.
notes: 4-coil Shakti layout: the left stereo channel's two coils on the left temporal lobe (FT7, TP7) and the right channel's two on the right (FT8, TP8), static, with no rotation or alternation; the vendor says only 'left channel coils on the left side, right channel on the right' (temporal or temporo-frontal), so the sites are an inference. The vendor gives no coil polarity for this 4-coil layout (the one + and one − coil per pair is documented only for the 8 Coil Shakti), so both coils of a side are driven with the same polarity here. Murphy says the slow signal keeps the 'same EEG pattern (long-term potentiating)' but changes 'the duration of the bursts ... as well as the length of time between the bursts'; its file (tp_24_16) is unpublished. Approximations: the amygdala 'burstx' file is approximated by the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz), 230 points of 3 ms (0.69 s, the published 230-point burst-firing length at Shakti's standard 3-ms points), then the standard 4 s of silence; the slow hippocampal signal by the project's standard LTP stand-in (4 theta bursts of 4 biphasic pulses) played on 4-ms points instead of 3, so the bursts and the time between them are a third longer (pulses 12 ms apart, bursts every 248 ms, about 4 Hz, a 0.99-s train), then 4 s of silence; the same choice as the project's Limbic Workout. The vendor does not say whether this form runs in sequence or at the same time; here both sides play at once, each with its own 4-s silence, so their onsets drift apart and back together. Standard forms: murphy-shakti-amyl-hippr-variants-sequence and murphy-shakti-amyl-hippr-variants-sync. Murphy aims the left amygdala signal at positive emotion and the right hippocampal signal at positive cognition, a vendor reading extended from small Persinger-lab studies (Persinger, Richards & Koren 1994: LTP-pattern fields over the right hemisphere were rated more pleasant than over the left). Murphy reports male users feeling 'energized' and describing better 'verbal/mathematical/logical skills'; these are testimonials. One negative report followed sessions longer than suggested, so keep to 30 min and the schedule. Murphy reports headache or pressure in about 2% of users of an earlier version of the technology, mostly with hippocampal signals; if so, lower the intensity by one third. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012, the latter with the 8 Coil Shakti amygdala signal). Not for people with epilepsy; stop at once if distressed.
